lessons_learned.lesson: Two approval receipts do not replace the separate final publication decision.
A corrected commit requires a new RC tag and fresh reviews; keep rejected RC refs for audit.
Bind reviews to code, frozen report and policy; a review count alone cannot authorize promotion.
An existing stable ref reserves its version; never adopt, move or delete a conflicting ref.
Persist publication intent before effects, then GET the exact tag and Release after lost responses; do not repeat a blind POST.
Compare versions numerically and distinguish the original operator, real account identity and run attempt.
A journal writer must recompute from fresh state after a CAS conflict, preserving the other approver receipt.
An unsuccessful preview cannot become a reviewable frozen report or a publication authorization.
Recheck effective protections after human waiting and before each external effect; preserve an already-created stable tag if protections disappear.
Offline fixtures prove helper behavior only; repeat human reviews, permissions and GitHub publication checks on the real service.

limitations: Synthetic reviews are not human E2E evidence.
Local correction is not a remote reviewed PR.
Preview HTTP success is fixture input, not a live Pages check.
Offline API cannot prove real GitHub permissions or UI behavior.
No mobile build, Shorebird patch, store or tester distribution.
